questions.title: Unnamed factors
questions.question: Does the prose use vague category nouns such as factors, aspects, considerations, or issues in place of the concrete subject of its claim, without identifying those items in the supplied text?
questions.guidance: Name the relevant items already supported by the text, or flag the missing detail instead of inventing it.

questions.title: Unspecified improvement
questions.question: Does the prose claim an improvement or optimization without saying what changed in behavior, capability, or a named measure?
questions.guidance: Describe the supported before-and-after behavior; retain uncertainty and do not invent measurements.

questions.title: Empty intensifiers
questions.question: Does a word such as truly, genuinely, incredibly, or very amplify praise without contributing a specific degree or meaningful contrast?
questions.guidance: Remove the intensifier if the underlying claim keeps its meaning.

questions.title: Unexplained authenticity
questions.question: Does real, actual, genuine, or true modify an abstract benefit merely to imply authenticity, with no named contrast or literal factual distinction?
questions.guidance: Drop the modifier or explain the contrast using information already supplied.

questions.title: Importance windup
questions.question: Does the prose announce that a fact is important to note or worth noting before stating it, where deleting that announcement would preserve the information?
questions.guidance: State the fact directly; retain any substantive reason it matters.

questions.title: Wordy purpose phrase
questions.question: Does the prose use in order to where to alone conveys exactly the same purpose?
questions.guidance: Replace in order to with to when the meaning is unchanged.

questions.title: Wordy causal phrase
questions.question: Does the prose use due to the fact that or owing to the fact that where because would express the same cause?
questions.guidance: Use because, retaining the original causal claim and its uncertainty.

questions.title: Wordy time phrase
questions.question: Does the prose use at this point in time or at the present time where now preserves the intended time reference?
questions.guidance: Use now or the supplied date, without changing the time being described.

questions.title: Wordy conditional phrase
questions.question: Does the prose use in the event that where if alone expresses the same condition?
questions.guidance: Use if and keep the condition intact.

questions.title: Wordy ability phrase
questions.question: Does the prose use has the ability to or is able to where can expresses the same capability, without a meaningful emphasis on demonstrated ability?
questions.guidance: Use can if it preserves the distinction between capability and actual performance.

questions.title: Redundant possibility hedges
questions.question: Does the prose stack equivalent possibility markers such as may potentially or could possibly on one claim, rather than expressing distinct probability and timing qualifications?
questions.guidance: Keep the hedge needed for accuracy and remove only the redundant possibility marker.

questions.title: Recommendation buried in hedging
questions.question: Does the prose bury an explicit recommendation under it might be worth considering whether or equivalent tentative framing, without stating a substantive uncertainty?
questions.guidance: State the recommendation directly while preserving any actual uncertainty or optionality.

questions.title: Inflated identification verb
questions.question: Does serves as, stands as, or represents merely identify what something is, with no role, symbolism, or temporary function that the verb needs to convey?
questions.guidance: Use is or are only when the richer verb contributes no meaning.

questions.title: Boastful possession
questions.question: Does boasts describe possession of an ordinary feature in otherwise descriptive prose, adding praise rather than a meaningful claim about boasting?
questions.guidance: Use has or describe the feature directly.

questions.title: Inflated use verbs
questions.question: Does utilize or leverage mean only use here, without a distinct technical meaning such as financial leverage or mechanical advantage?
questions.guidance: Use use where it preserves the meaning; retain genuine terms of art.

questions.title: Inflated corporate wording
questions.question: Does the prose use operationalize, functionality, or methodology where a simpler verb, feature, or method would carry the same specific meaning?
questions.guidance: Choose the simpler equivalent only when no technical distinction is lost.

questions.title: Ornate everyday actions
questions.question: Does commence, ascertain, or endeavor add formality without a distinct meaning that start, find out, or try would lack?
questions.guidance: Use the plain equivalent while retaining the intended degree of effort or certainty.

questions.title: Cliched exploration framing
questions.question: Does delve into, embark on a journey, or take a deep dive serve as generic framing for explaining a topic, rather than describe literal exploration or a meaningful depth of analysis?
questions.guidance: Start with the subject or the specific analysis being undertaken.

questions.title: Abstract scenery metaphor
questions.question: Does a metaphor such as a tapestry, landscape, realm, or symphony substitute decorative scenery for a concrete account of the topic's relationships?
questions.guidance: State the relationships supported by the text; preserve literal uses and informative metaphors.

questions.title: Stock breakthrough claim
questions.question: Does pushes the boundaries, unlocks the full potential, game changer, or paradigm shift praise a development without identifying the specific new capability or change?
questions.guidance: Describe the actual change from the supplied evidence or remove the stock praise.

questions.title: Unspecified quality label
questions.question: Does robust, seamless, comprehensive, or meticulous function as unqualified praise without naming the resilience, integration, coverage, or care it describes?
questions.guidance: State the relevant property already known; keep technical meanings and supported descriptions.

questions.title: Complexity without content
questions.question: Does intricate, holistic, or complexities substitute for describing which parts or relationships make the subject complex?
questions.guidance: Name the relevant parts or relationships from the supplied text.

questions.title: Clustered business buzzwords
questions.question: Does a paragraph cluster at least two inflated business verbs or labels such as empower, foster, elevate, harness, catalyze, multifaceted, or ecosystem without explaining the actions or relationships they describe?
questions.guidance: Replace the cluster with specific supported actions; retain literal and necessary technical uses.

questions.title: Dense generic praise
questions.question: Does a paragraph repeatedly rely on generic praise such as innovative, effective, compelling, remarkable, or sophisticated instead of explaining the properties being praised?
questions.guidance: Cut repeated praise and retain the specific properties already supported.

questions.title: Repeated sector boilerplate
questions.question: Does the text repeatedly use the same vague phrase such as emerging sector, long-term sustainability, or user engagement without specifying what it means in that context?
questions.guidance: Name the sector, time constraint, or user action when supplied; otherwise flag the gap.

questions.title: Clustered sector boilerplate
questions.question: Does the text combine three or more vague stock phrases such as at the intersection of, community-driven, long-term sustainability, tokenized incentives, or emerging space without explaining their concrete meaning?
questions.guidance: Replace the generic cluster with the supported mechanism or claim.

questions.title: Generic step-forward claim
questions.question: Does a step forward or a step toward framing praise progress without saying what capability or outcome actually changed?
questions.guidance: State the concrete change, or remove the progress framing.

questions.title: Generic audience extremes
questions.question: Does a whether you are X or Y construction invoke broad audience extremes merely to imply everyone, without giving either audience a distinct relevant benefit?
questions.guidance: Name the intended audience if supplied, or remove the audience framing.

questions.title: Stock pleasure announcement
questions.question: Does I had the pleasure of introduce an encounter or activity as a ceremonial windup without adding a meaningful personal reaction?
questions.guidance: State what happened; preserve an actual personal response when it contributes to the piece.

questions.title: Repeated additive transitions
questions.question: Do successive sentences repeatedly start with Additionally, Furthermore, Moreover, or In addition where the connection is already clear and no distinct logical relationship is added?
questions.guidance: Join related points or remove redundant transitions; keep transitions that clarify the logic.

questions.title: Generic era opener
questions.question: Does the prose open with generic era framing such as in today's rapidly changing world rather than name a specific relevant circumstance?
questions.guidance: Lead with the actual claim or the specific circumstance already provided.

questions.title: Unearned reader steering
questions.question: Does a phrase such as here is the interesting part pre-label the next statement as interesting without explaining what makes it relevant or unexpected?
questions.guidance: Present the fact and its supported significance directly.

questions.title: Redundant summary announcement
questions.question: Does in conclusion, to summarize, or in summary add only a ceremonial announcement to a short passage whose conclusion is already obvious?
questions.guidance: Remove the announcement when the conclusion remains clear.

questions.title: Generic topic windup
questions.question: Does when it comes to, in terms of, or at the end of the day delay the point without carrying a specific relationship or literal time meaning?
questions.guidance: Start with the topic or claim itself.

questions.title: Repeated concession transitions
questions.question: Does the prose repeatedly use that said, that being said, or similar concession transitions without making a meaningful contrast each time?
questions.guidance: Keep only transitions that express an actual concession or contrast.

questions.title: Inflated historical significance
questions.question: Does the prose call an event pivotal, a watershed, or historically transformative without describing any corresponding consequence in the supplied text?
questions.guidance: Describe the event and known consequence; do not invent historical importance.

questions.title: Superficial participial analysis
questions.question: Does a trailing highlighting, underscoring, symbolizing, or showcasing clause add vague importance rather than a concrete consequence or supported interpretation?
questions.guidance: Remove the empty tail or state its supported consequence directly.

questions.title: Unsupported symbolic gloss
questions.question: Does a declarative gloss such as this reflects a broader shift or symbolizes a commitment add vague significance without explaining the specific shift or commitment?
questions.guidance: Describe the observable change or omit the gloss.

questions.title: Manufactured aphorism
questions.question: Does a formula such as X is the currency of Y or the architecture of trust present a vague metaphor as a general law without explaining a concrete relationship?
questions.guidance: State the actual relationship; retain attributed quotations and established idioms used meaningfully.

questions.title: Untestable future narrative
questions.question: Does the prose predict that something will become a defining narrative, major chapter, or important trend without specifying an observable change or condition?
questions.guidance: State an existing testable prediction if supplied, or remove the empty forecast.

questions.title: Generic upbeat ending
questions.question: Does the passage end with an upbeat formula such as the future looks bright, exciting times lie ahead, or a journey toward excellence that adds no concrete next step or conclusion?
questions.guidance: End on the last substantive claim or an already-supported next step.

questions.title: Empty uncertainty closer
questions.question: Does only time will tell or as we move forward close the discussion without naming the uncertainty or what would resolve it?
questions.guidance: Name the unresolved question if the text supplies it, or omit the closer.

questions.title: Decorative negative foil
questions.question: Does a not X but Y or not just X construction reject a vague or self-evident foil merely for emphasis, rather than rule out a specific plausible alternative?
questions.guidance: State the positive claim directly; preserve contrasts that distinguish real alternatives.

questions.title: Split negative reveal
questions.question: Do consecutive sentences stage a reveal by denying vague alternatives before announcing the real point, without the denials conveying useful distinctions?
questions.guidance: Lead with the substantive positive point and retain only informative exclusions.

questions.title: Tacked-on negative flourish
questions.question: Does a bare tail such as no guessing or no compromises add a slogan-like negation to a sentence without specifying a real constraint?
questions.guidance: Remove the flourish or express the supported constraint as a clear clause; keep genuine constraint lists.

questions.title: Needless double negative
questions.question: Does a double negative such as not unimportant or not uncommon obscure a simple affirmative claim without preserving a deliberate qualification?
questions.guidance: Use the direct equivalent only if its strength matches the original claim.

questions.title: Repeated padded triads
questions.question: Does the prose repeatedly arrange praise into three-part lists whose items overlap in meaning or add no distinct information, rather than enumerate three real items?
questions.guidance: Remove redundant items and keep whatever number of distinct points the content supports.

questions.title: False range
questions.question: Does a from X to Y construction imply comprehensive breadth between unrelated endpoints without a meaningful scale, chronology, or stated organizing dimension?
questions.guidance: List the actual topics or identify the meaningful dimension if the text provides one.

questions.title: Hollow concession
questions.question: Does a while X is impressive but Y is challenging construction simulate balance while leaving both the benefit and the limitation unspecified?
questions.guidance: Name the supported benefit and limitation, or remove the empty balancing frame.

questions.title: Undefined mirrored contrast
questions.question: Does the prose pair a concrete concept with a vague invented-sounding opposite solely for verbal symmetry, without explaining how the two differ?
questions.guidance: Explain the actual distinction or state the positive claim; do not assume an unfamiliar term is fabricated.

questions.title: Moralized technical property
questions.question: Does honest, faithful, or truthful describe an inanimate technical property without a clear meaning such as representational fidelity, accuracy, or disclosure?
questions.guidance: Name the intended technical property; keep established uses such as faithful reproduction when precise.

questions.title: Sweeping consensus appeal
questions.question: Does the text appeal to what everyone knows or what every expert teaches as authority without specifying a source or relevant scope?
questions.guidance: Remove the sweeping appeal or give the scope already supported; do not invent a citation.

questions.title: Brochure-like description
questions.question: Does otherwise informative prose describe a place or product with stacked promotional praise such as breathtaking, vibrant, renowned, or must-visit instead of relevant descriptive facts?
questions.guidance: Use the supported description and preserve any explicitly requested advertising voice.

questions.title: Formulaic resilience
questions.question: Does a despite challenges continues to thrive sentence claim resilience without naming either the challenge or the response?
questions.guidance: State the known challenge and response or remove the sentence.

questions.title: Speculative world opener
questions.question: Does imagine a world or picture a future substitute a list of desirable outcomes for an argument, outside fiction or a concrete teaching thought experiment?
questions.guidance: State the substantive claim and supported implications without the generic scenario.

questions.title: Prestige without context
questions.question: Does the prose list prestigious outlets, institutions, or people solely to establish importance without explaining what they said or did that matters here?
questions.guidance: Keep the specific relevant attribution; remove prestige lists that add no information.

questions.title: Stacked historical analogies
questions.question: Does the prose pile up analogies to major past inventions or companies without explaining the relevant similarity for any one of them?
questions.guidance: Keep only an analogy whose supported mechanism helps explain the claim.

questions.title: Unnamed authority
questions.question: Does the prose attribute a claim to studies, experts, observers, or researchers without identifying any source in the supplied text, excluding explicitly anonymized participants?
questions.guidance: Identify the source if available; otherwise flag the missing attribution instead of manufacturing one.

questions.title: Faceless external validation
questions.question: Does the prose claim independent testing or third-party validation establishes superiority without naming a test, report, auditor, or other checkable source?
questions.guidance: Supply the existing test and result, or flag the claim as needing evidence.

questions.title: Proof stronger than stated evidence
questions.question: Does the prose claim proof or certainty from evidence it explicitly describes as limited observations, a small sample, or anecdotal reports?
questions.guidance: Match the conclusion's certainty to the evidence actually described.

questions.title: Unbounded superiority claim
questions.question: Does the prose claim best, only, or universal superiority while its own stated comparison covers only a limited named set of alternatives or conditions?
questions.guidance: Limit the claim to the comparison and conditions actually reported.

questions.title: Unsupported nobody-knows hook
questions.question: Does the prose claim nobody talks about, nobody is naming, or everyone is missing a topic as an engagement hook without identifying a specific knowledge gap?
questions.guidance: Describe the issue directly; preserve a specific supported gap and avoid asserting novelty without verification.

questions.title: Unexplained coined label
questions.question: Does the prose introduce a novel-sounding compound label for a problem or principle without defining what mechanism or distinction the label means?
questions.guidance: Explain the mechanism already present or use ordinary descriptive wording.

questions.title: Manufactured reveal hook
questions.question: Does a standalone hook such as the kicker, the catch, plot twist, or here is the thing manufacture suspense before an ordinary point without a rhetorical purpose in the stated voice?
questions.guidance: State the point directly while retaining deliberate storytelling when requested.

questions.title: Theatrical candor hook
questions.question: Does a standalone honestly, real talk, or let's be honest stage a reveal without adding substantive disclosure or a meaningful conversational response?
questions.guidance: Remove the theatrical setup and preserve the substantive disclosure.

questions.title: Reason-free recommendation
questions.question: Does a recommendation such as worth your time, must-read, bookmark this, or thank me later urge attention without giving a specific reason or relevant audience?
questions.guidance: Keep a supplied reason for recommending the item, or let the item stand without generic endorsement.

questions.title: Emotion as a transition
questions.question: Does a phrase such as what surprised me most or I was fascinated to discover serve only as a transition without explaining the surprise or reaction?
questions.guidance: Present the observation or preserve a supported personal reaction; never invent feelings.

questions.title: Unexplained lingering attention
questions.question: Does the writer say they keep coming back to or cannot stop thinking about something without saying what about it holds their attention?
questions.guidance: Lead with the idea or the supplied reason it recurs; do not invent a personal history.

questions.title: Rhetorical question windup
questions.question: Does a question such as why should you care or what does this mean function only as a transition immediately answered by the next claim, rather than pose a real question or useful teaching prompt?
questions.guidance: State the answer directly unless the question serves the intended argument or teaching style.

questions.title: Empty nuanced aside
questions.question: Does a parenthetical such as and perhaps more importantly add only a performance of nuance without a substantive qualification?
questions.guidance: Cut the empty aside; retain or separately state qualifications that change the claim.

questions.title: Chatbot delivery preface
questions.question: Does finished prose contain a delivery preface such as here is the essay you requested or certainly here is an overview, outside an actual conversational response?
questions.guidance: Remove the delivery wrapper from the artifact itself.

questions.title: Chatbot service signoff
questions.question: Does finished prose include I hope this helps or let me know if you need anything else as an assistant-service signoff, outside genuine correspondence where it serves the exchange?
questions.guidance: Remove the assistant-service signoff from the prose artifact.

questions.title: False collaborative transition
questions.question: Does let's explore, let's examine, or let's break this down function only as a transition rather than a real invitation or instructional step?
questions.guidance: Start with the substantive point; keep genuine joint actions and teaching instructions.

questions.title: Internal reasoning scaffold
questions.question: Does finished prose contain let me think step by step, here is my thought process, or similar narration of the assistant's drafting process rather than a reader-facing explanation?
questions.guidance: Present the conclusion and relevant rationale; retain actual procedural instructions.

questions.title: Generic reader flattery
questions.question: Does the prose lavish generic praise on the reader or their question, such as absolutely brilliant question, without a specific substantive assessment?
questions.guidance: Remove the generic praise and answer or assess the substance directly.

questions.title: Narrating one's candor
questions.question: Does the prose announce the writer's own transparency or bravery before disclosing a limitation, where that announcement can be removed without losing the disclosure or a required conflict-of-interest label?
questions.guidance: State the limitation directly; preserve material admissions and conventional conflict disclosures.

questions.title: Prompt restatement
questions.question: Does the opening merely restate a visible question or request before answering it, without disambiguating the request or adding useful context?
questions.guidance: Answer directly; keep restatements that resolve ambiguity.

questions.title: Praise disguised as recap
questions.question: Does a reply begin by recapping the recipient's work at length as praise before reaching its own point, rather than give a brief relevant thank-you?
questions.guidance: Lead with the response; retain a brief genuine acknowledgment if appropriate.

questions.title: Repeated significance cues
questions.question: Does the prose repeatedly preface facts with notably, importantly, interestingly, or undoubtedly to dictate their significance instead of explaining it?
questions.guidance: Remove repeated cues and preserve any specific explanation of importance or uncertainty.

questions.title: Announced profundity
questions.question: Does at its core, make no mistake, the truth is, or the real question is announce authority or depth without contributing a substantive distinction?
questions.guidance: State the claim directly, retaining any actual distinction.

questions.title: Self-labeled cleverness
questions.question: Does a sentence point back to the last item or move and label it clever, contrarian, or surprising without explaining why?
questions.guidance: Remove the label or connect the item to the supported reason it matters.

questions.title: Training-cutoff artifact
questions.question: Does a prose artifact refer to the model's training cutoff or lack of browsing access as residual assistant narration, outside a relevant disclosure about the tool itself?
questions.guidance: Remove the artifact from finished prose while preserving a truthful limitation wherever it is relevant.

questions.title: Acknowledged gap filled by guess
questions.question: Does the text acknowledge that a biographical or historical fact is unknown and then supply a plausible guess as background without evidence or an explicit hypothesis purpose?
questions.guidance: Retain the uncertainty and remove the unsupported guessed detail; do not fabricate a replacement.

questions.title: Unfilled publishing placeholder
questions.question: Does prose presented as finished contain a slot such as INSERT SOURCE, Your Name, or a date with XX fields that is not part of an intentional template or example?
questions.guidance: Fill the slot only from verified information, or flag it as unresolved.

questions.title: Internal citation markup
questions.question: Does the prose contain internal chat citation tokens such as contentReference, oaicite, or turn0search0 outside a discussion or example of those tokens?
questions.guidance: Replace leaked markup with the actual supported reference; do not delete meaningful attribution.

questions.title: Assistant tracking parameter
questions.question: Does an authored hyperlink include an unnecessary AI-tool tracking parameter such as utm_source=chatgpt.com, excluding a quoted or instructional URL example?
questions.guidance: Remove only the unnecessary tracking parameter and preserve the destination and functional query parameters.

questions.title: Argument fragmented into bullets
questions.question: Does a bullet list split a single connected argument or sentence into dependent fragments, instead of enumerating independent items or steps?
questions.guidance: Restore the relationships in prose while preserving true lists and required formatting.

questions.title: Bare praise bullet stack
questions.question: Does a run of at least five short bullets list vague adjective-noun praises with no checkable claims, rather than actual options, ingredients, parameters, or checklist items?
questions.guidance: Remove redundant praise or express supported distinct claims; keep genuine enumerations.

questions.title: Repeated inline label
questions.question: Does a list item start with a short header and immediately repeat that header's content in its explanation without adding information?
questions.guidance: Remove the repeated lead-in or write the item as a direct claim.

questions.title: Padded numbered list
questions.question: Does a numbered list include substantively duplicate or empty items apparently to meet its announced count rather than enumerate distinct points?
questions.guidance: Merge duplicate items and keep only distinct supported points.

questions.title: Mechanical bold emphasis
questions.question: Does running prose repeatedly bold ordinary phrases without an apparent navigation, definition, interface-label, or contrast function?
questions.guidance: Remove decorative emphasis while retaining useful labels and intentional formatting.

questions.title: Decorative heading emoji
questions.question: Do formal prose headings contain decorative emoji that are not necessary symbols, quoted labels, or part of an explicitly requested visual style?
questions.guidance: Remove the decoration while preserving meaningful symbols and required labels.

questions.title: Repeated prose dash splices
questions.question: Does the passage repeatedly interrupt or splice prose with em dashes, en dashes, or double hyphens where the interruptions obscure the relationships, excluding ranges, names, and list-label separators?
questions.guidance: Use punctuation or sentence boundaries that express the actual relationships; retain intentional effective dashes.

questions.title: Formal dash preference
questions.question: Does formal running prose use an em dash, en dash, or double hyphen as an aside or clause splice, rather than a numeric range, paired name, or list-label separator?
questions.guidance: Consider a comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses consistent with the intended relationship.

questions.title: Stacked compound modifiers
questions.question: Does a noun carry multiple hyphenated promotional modifiers such as future-proof and best-in-class that pile up praise instead of distinguishing the thing described?
questions.guidance: Keep only meaningful supported modifiers; preserve standard technical compounds.

questions.title: Heading repeated as warmup
questions.question: Does a heading have a following warmup sentence that merely restates it before the substantive content begins?
questions.guidance: Remove the warmup when the heading already provides its information.

questions.title: Overfragmented short passage
questions.question: Does a short prose passage divide connected thoughts among several tiny headed sections whose headings add no navigational or informational value?
questions.guidance: Combine related sections while preserving required templates and useful navigation.

questions.title: Documentation anchored to a diff
questions.question: Does reference documentation describe what was just added or replaced instead of the current behavior, outside release notes, migration guides, decision records, or other intentionally historical documents?
questions.guidance: Describe the current behavior and its reason, keeping necessary version history where it belongs.

questions.title: Repeated dramatic fragments
questions.question: Does the paragraph stack three or more similarly shaped clipped fragments for manufactured dramatic emphasis rather than use a deliberate voice, genuine list, or terse reference format?
questions.guidance: Combine redundant fragments into natural sentences while preserving intentional rhythm.

questions.title: Repeated sentence template
questions.question: Do at least three consecutive prose sentences repeat the same opening and grammatical frame without an intentional parallel argument, emphasis, or reference-list purpose?
questions.guidance: Vary or combine sentences where useful; retain stable technical terminology.

questions.title: Monotonous sentence rhythm
questions.question: Do at least four sentences repeat nearly the same length and clause structure in a way that makes the paragraph mechanically repetitive, outside deliberately parallel instructions?
questions.guidance: Vary sentence structure through meaning-preserving combinations or splits; do not manufacture fragments.

questions.title: Uniform paragraph template
questions.question: Do at least three body paragraphs repeat the same opening-development-summary template with redundant material, rather than follow a required or useful parallel structure?
questions.guidance: Keep each paragraph's contribution and remove redundant template material.

questions.title: Redundant paragraph closer
questions.question: Does the last sentence of a short body paragraph merely restate its preceding claim without adding a consequence, qualification, or useful recap?
questions.guidance: Remove the closer if the paragraph retains its point and necessary transition.

questions.title: Paragraph adds no information
questions.question: Does a body paragraph merely paraphrase a preceding paragraph without adding a fact, reason, qualification, example, or purposeful recap?
questions.guidance: Remove or merge the repetition while preserving deliberate summaries where needed.

questions.title: Missing argument connection
questions.question: Does a passage presented as a connected argument jump between body paragraphs without explaining a relationship necessary to follow its conclusion, excluding independent reference sections?
questions.guidance: State the relationship already supported by the argument, or reorganize it; do not invent a causal link.

questions.title: Passive hides a known actor
questions.question: Does a passive construction obscure responsibility or agency even though the relevant actor is explicitly known from the supplied text and naming it would clarify the claim?
questions.guidance: Use that known actor as the subject; retain passive voice when the actor is irrelevant or unknown.

questions.title: Ambiguous subjectless prose
questions.question: Does flowing prose omit a grammatical subject in a way that makes who acts unclear, outside headings, labels, instructions, or intentionally terse reference entries?
questions.guidance: Name the actor supported by the context; do not invent an actor.

questions.title: Broken parallel grammar
questions.question: Does a coordinated list or series of predicates mix grammatical forms so that one item no longer fits the sentence's shared lead-in?
questions.guidance: Put equivalent items in compatible grammatical forms without changing their roles.

questions.title: Long subject-verb interruption
questions.question: Does a long inserted clause separate the main subject from its verb enough to make the main statement hard to follow?
questions.guidance: Move the insertion or split the sentence while retaining every material qualification.

questions.title: Ambiguous modifier attachment
questions.question: Does a modifier sit far enough from what it describes that it can plausibly attach to the wrong subject or action?
questions.guidance: Move the modifier beside its intended referent, preserving the original meaning.

questions.title: Main result loses emphasis
questions.question: Does a sentence state its main result in the middle and then trail off into already-given background that weakens the result's clarity, rather than add an essential qualification?
questions.guidance: Reorder the sentence to emphasize the result while retaining necessary conditions.

questions.title: Overloaded long sentence
questions.question: Does a sentence longer than about thirty words combine multiple separable claims or nested qualifications that make it hard to follow?
questions.guidance: Split at natural claim boundaries, keeping all conditions and relationships; retain a long sentence that is one clear logical unit.

questions.title: Unhelpful synonym cycling
questions.question: Does the prose rotate several names for the same entity or concept in a way that makes them seem like different things, rather than distinguish real roles or meanings?
questions.guidance: Reuse the clearest established term and keep distinctions that are real.

questions.title: Repeated abbreviation definition
questions.question: Does a continuous document redefine the same abbreviation unnecessarily after it has already been established, excluding standalone sections that need their own definitions?
questions.guidance: Use the established abbreviation and preserve definitions needed for independent reading.

questions.title: Unexplained acronym pileup
questions.question: Does a sentence pile up specialized acronyms essential to its meaning without definitions or contextual explanation for the explicitly supplied intended audience? Answer no if no audience is supplied or that audience can reasonably know them.
questions.guidance: Define only terms that the stated audience needs; preserve standard domain vocabulary.

questions.title: Mechanics without stated purpose
questions.question: Does a self-contained explanatory passage list implementation mechanics without stating what they accomplish, where that purpose is needed to understand the passage and is not already supplied by context?
questions.guidance: Lead with the purpose already known or flag it for the author; do not infer an unsupported purpose.

questions.title: Formal contraction preference
questions.question: Does formal prose use a grammatical contraction such as can't, doesn't, or we're outside quoted speech, a proper name, or an explicitly requested informal voice?
questions.guidance: Consider the full form for formal register; preserve quoted language and intended informal voice.

questions.title: Opt-in causal so preference
questions.question: Does the prose join independent clauses with comma so, or use so that as a causal splice, rather than use so as an intensifier, fixed phrase, or genuine purpose construction?
questions.guidance: Under this opt-in preference, split the clauses or clarify their causal relationship without changing it.
